statement: A polynomial $f$ of degree $2$ satisfies $f(x+1)-f(x)=2x+1$ and $f(0)=0$. Find $f(x)$.
solution: Let $f(x)=ax^{2}+bx+c$ with $f(0)=0$, so $c=0$. Then $f(x+1)-f(x)=a(x+1)^{2}+b(x+1)-ax^{2}-bx=a(2x+1)+b=2ax+(a+b)$. Equating to $2x+1$ gives $2a=2$ so $a=1$, and $a+b=1$ so $b=0$. Hence $f(x)=x^{2}$.
hints: Write f as ax^2+bx+c and use f(0)=0.
